content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Per-session registry that hydrates proxied upstream tools onto the
3	 * `McpServer` alongside the built-ins.
4	 *
5	 * Lifecycle:
6	 *   - `init(server)` runs once per session in `McpSessionDO.init()`.
7	 *     It enumerates upstreams the caller can reach (visibility +
8	 *     credentials), decrypts each bearer, ensures the catalogue cache
9	 *     is fresh, and registers one mangled MCP tool per cached
10	 *     `upstream_tools` row.
11	 *   - Tool handlers dispatch through the cached `UpstreamClient` via
12	 *     `upstream-call-runner.ts`, or through `async-submit.ts` for
13	 *     tools on the upstream's `authConfig.asyncTools`.
14	 *   - An upstream whose per-user credential is on file but unusable (dead
15	 *     = reauth-required, or a refresh that failed just now) is LISTED
16	 *     anyway, from the cached catalogue, with no client bound. Its calls
17	 *     fail loudly with first-party recovery text instead of the tools
18	 *     silently vanishing — an agent with no tools improvises, an agent
19	 *     with a failing tool reports why (2026-09-17 field finding). The
20	 *     handler binds a client on demand (`ensureBound`), so once the user
21	 *     re-authorizes in the browser the very next call works: the tool
22	 *     list never changed, so no `tools/list_changed` round-trip and no
23	 *     client reconnect is involved.
24	 *   - There is no teardown: sessions are short-lived and the workerd
25	 *     isolate frees Client state on its own when the DO dies.
26	 *
27	 * Catalogue freshness: a row older than `CATALOGUE_TTL_SECONDS` is
28	 * refreshed inline on first session encounter — accepted as a one-time
29	 * connect cost so the agent sees a complete `tools/list` immediately.
30	 * Empty cache (brand-new upstream) is also refreshed inline.
31	 *
32	 * The read-models behind `describe_upstream` / `list_upstreams` /
33	 * `restrictedTools` live in `catalogue-views.ts`.
34	 */
35	
36	import type { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js'
37	import type { Env } from '../env'
38	import {
39	  toUpstreamConnection,
40	  type UpstreamConnection,
41	  type UpstreamServerRow
42	} from '../db/queries/upstreams'
43	import { listCachedTools, listCachedToolsForUpstreams, replaceCachedTools, type UpstreamToolRow } from '../db/queries/upstream-tools'

89	/**
90	 * How long a stale-catalogue refresh may hold up registration before the
91	 * cached catalogue is served instead. Session `init()` runs inside the DO's
92	 * `blockConcurrencyWhile`, which the runtime cancels at ~30 s and answers by
93	 * RESETTING the object — so one hung upstream used to take the whole session

95	 * minutes per call). The per-call listTools timeout (60 s) is far past that
96	 * window, hence a separate, much tighter budget here. The refresh is not
97	 * abandoned: it keeps running and heals the cache for the next session.

175	  /**
176	   * Hydrate the registry and register one MCP tool per cached upstream
177	   * tool. Safe to call before any built-in tools are registered — the
178	   * SDK accumulates handlers across calls and the eventual `tools/list`
179	   * returns the union. Accepts the prefetched per-user context from
180	   * `loadUserContext` (session init shares it with `upstreamGuidance`);
181	   * loads it itself when not supplied.
182	   */
183	  async init(server: McpServer, ctx?: UpstreamUserContext): Promise<void> {
184	    const { rows, skillsByUpstream, docsByUpstream } =
185	      ctx ?? (await loadUserContext(this.env, this.userId))
186	    await this.registerUpstreams(server, rows, skillsByUpstream, docsByUpstream)
187	  }

189	  /**
190	   * Re-scan the caller's upstreams and grow this session's registered
191	   * tool set to match reality:
192	   *   1. Register every tool of any upstream connected AFTER this
193	   *      session's `init` (a mid-session connect is otherwise invisible
194	   *      until the MCP client reconnects).
195	   *   2. Reconcile ALREADY-connected upstreams against the org-global
196	   *      catalogue — the cache may have been refreshed (or healed from a
197	   *      degraded `tools/list`) by another session/admin since this
198	   *      session registered, leaving this session bound to a subset
199	   *      (2026-08-11 Datadog incident: sessions stuck on 3 of 25 tools).
200	   *      Newly-visible allowed tools are registered; nothing is ever
201	   *      unregistered mid-session (ACL revocation is backstopped in the
202	   *      call handler instead).
203	   * Idempotent: already-registered tools are skipped, so no tool is
204	   * double-registered (registering a duplicate name would throw). Emits
205	   * `tools/list_changed` on the live server when something new registers —
206	   * a client that honors it surfaces the tools without a reconnect.
207	   * Returns a summary of what was added on either path.
208	   */
209	  async refresh(server: McpServer): Promise<RefreshSummary> {
210	    const { rows, skillsByUpstream, docsByUpstream } = await loadUserContext(this.env, this.userId)
211	    // "Fresh" = no live client: never-seen upstreams AND listed-but-unbound
212	    // ones (re-prepared here so a re-authorized credential binds now).
213	    const fresh = rows.filter((r) => !this.clients.has(r.id))
214	    const reg = await this.registerUpstreams(server, fresh, skillsByUpstream, docsByUpstream)
215	    const added = reg.added.filter((a) => a.tools > 0)
216	    added.push(
217	      ...(await this.reconcileConnected(
218	        server,
219	        rows.filter((r) => this.clients.has(r.id)),
220	        skillsByUpstream,
221	        docsByUpstream
222	      ))
223	    )
224	    // ALWAYS tell the client to re-read, not only when this call registered
225	    // something. The session DO hibernates; each wake rebuilds this registry
226	    // and re-runs init(), which silently registers whatever connected since —
227	    // so by the time the agent calls reload_upstreams the diff against THIS
228	    // instance is empty even though the client's tool list is stale
229	    // (2026-09-17 field report: an upstream went 0 → 79 tools, reload said
230	    // "nothing new", the tools surfaced only later). reload_upstreams is the
231	    // explicit "sync me" action; the notification is an idempotent re-fetch.
232	    try {
233	      server.server.sendToolListChanged()
234	    } catch (err) {
235	      console.error('[upstream-proxy] sendToolListChanged failed:', err)
236	    }
237	    return {
238	      added,
239	      recovered: reg.recovered,
240	      unbound: [...this.unbound.values()],
241	      loaded: this.clients.size
242	    }
243	  }
244	
245	  /**
246	   * Register tools that appeared in the catalogue after this session
247	   * bound an upstream (see `refresh` step 2). Re-runs the same
248	   * freshness check `init` used — `ensureCatalogue` dials only when the
249	   * cache is empty/stale, reusing this session's live client — then
250	   * registers every allowed tool not yet in `allowedToolKeys` (the
251	   * registered set). Per-upstream failures degrade only that upstream.
252	   */
253	  private async reconcileConnected(
254	    server: McpServer,
255	    rows: UpstreamServerRow[],
256	    skillsByUpstream: Map<string, SkillForUpstreamRow[]>,
257	    docsByUpstream: Map<string, DocForUpstreamRow[]>
258	  ): Promise<{ slug: string; tools: number }[]> {
259	    if (rows.length === 0) return []
260	    const [principals, aclRows, cachedByUpstream] = await Promise.all([
261	      resolveUserPrincipals(this.env, this.userId),
262	      listToolAccessForUpstreams(
263	        this.env,
264	        rows.map((r) => r.id)
265	      ),
266	      listCachedToolsForUpstreams(
267	        this.env,
268	        rows.map((r) => r.id)
269	      )
270	    ])
271	    const acl = indexToolAccess(aclRows)
272	    const out: { slug: string; tools: number }[] = []
273	    for (const row of rows) {
274	      try {
275	        const conn = safeConnection(row)
276	        if (!conn) continue
277	        const client = this.clients.get(conn.id)
278	        if (!client) continue
279	        const tools = await this.ensureCatalogue(conn, client, cachedByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? [])
280	        const perTool = perToolPointers(
281	          skillsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? [],
282	          docsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? []
283	        )
284	        this.armFirstResultHint(
285	          conn.id,
286	          conn.slug,
287	          skillsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? [],
288	          docsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? []
289	        )
290	        let count = 0
291	        for (const t of tools) {
292	          const key = accessKey(conn.id, t.tool_name)
293	          if (this.allowedToolKeys.has(key)) continue // registered this session
294	          if (!isToolAllowed(acl.get(key), principals)) continue // hidden by ACL
295	          this.allowedToolKeys.add(key)
296	          this.registerTool(server, conn, t, perTool.get(t.tool_name) ?? [])
297	          count++
298	        }
299	        if (count > 0) out.push({ slug: conn.slug, tools: count })
300	      } catch (err) {
301	        console.error(`[upstream-proxy] ${row.slug}: reconcile failed: ${errMessage(err)}`)
302	      }
303	    }
304	    return out
305	  }

307	  /**
308	   * Prepare + register one MCP tool per allowed cached tool for the given
309	   * upstream rows. Shared by `init` (all visible upstreams) and `refresh`
310	   * (only the newly-connected ones). Returns per-upstream registered-tool
311	   * counts in `rows` order — registration is sequential so `tools/list`
312	   * stays deterministic.
313	   */
314	  private async registerUpstreams(
315	    server: McpServer,
316	    rows: UpstreamServerRow[],
317	    skillsByUpstream: Map<string, SkillForUpstreamRow[]>,
318	    docsByUpstream: Map<string, DocForUpstreamRow[]>
319	  ): Promise<{ added: { slug: string; tools: number }[]; recovered: string[] }> {
320	    if (rows.length === 0) return { added: [], recovered: [] }
321	    // Resolve the caller's principals + the per-tool ACL + the cached
322	    // catalogues for every visible upstream once, up front. A tool with
323	    // no ACL rows inherits the upstream's visibility; a locked tool the
324	    // caller doesn't match is HIDDEN here (never registered, so the agent
325	    // never sees it). The allowed-key set also backstops the call handler.
326	    const [principals, aclRows, cachedByUpstream] = await Promise.all([
327	      resolveUserPrincipals(this.env, this.userId),
328	      listToolAccessForUpstreams(
329	        this.env,
330	        rows.map((r) => r.id)
331	      ),
332	      listCachedToolsForUpstreams(
333	        this.env,
334	        rows.map((r) => r.id)
335	      )
336	    ])
337	    const acl = indexToolAccess(aclRows)
338	    // Per-upstream prep (bearer resolution, client dial, catalogue
339	    // refresh) runs concurrently; a throw degrades only that upstream.
340	    // Registration happens sequentially afterwards, in `rows` order, so
341	    // the tool ordering visible in `tools/list` stays deterministic.
342	    const prepped = await Promise.all(
343	      rows.map((row) =>
344	        this.prepareUpstream(row, cachedByUpstream.get(row.id) ?? []).catch((err) => {
345	          const msg = errMessage(err)
346	          console.error(`[upstream-proxy] ${row.slug}: init failed: ${msg}`)
347	          return null
348	        })
349	      )
350	    )
351	    // One batched read of the credential stamps the freshly-bound clients
352	    // were resolved under (see `boundStamp`).
353	    const stampIds = prepped.flatMap((p) => (p?.client && isUserScoped(p.conn) ? [p.conn.id] : []))
354	    const stamps =
355	      stampIds.length > 0
356	        ? await getUserCredentialStatuses(this.env, this.userId, stampIds)
357	        : new Map<string, CredentialStatus>()
358	    const added: { slug: string; tools: number }[] = []
359	    const recovered: string[] = []
360	    for (const prep of prepped) {
361	      if (!prep) continue
362	      const { conn, row, client, tools } = prep
363	      this.rows.set(conn.id, row)
364	      if (client) {
365	        this.clients.set(conn.id, client)
366	        this.boundStamp.set(conn.id, stamps.get(conn.id)?.updatedAt ?? null)
367	        if (this.unbound.delete(conn.id)) recovered.push(conn.slug)
368	      } else {
369	        this.unbound.set(conn.id, conn.slug)
370	      }
371	      const skills = skillsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? []
372	      const docs = docsByUpstream.get(conn.id) ?? []
373	      this.armFirstResultHint(conn.id, conn.slug, skills, docs)
374	      // Only PER-TOOL pointers (tool_name != '') ride the description now.
375	      // Whole-upstream playbooks (tool_name = '') are NOT fanned onto every
376	      // tool anymore — they already live in the server `instructions`
377	      // (`upstreamGuidance`) and in `list_upstreams.attached_skills`, so
378	      // repeating them on each tool was redundant noise. Per-tool bindings also
379	      // have a structured home in `describe_upstream`; this description line is
380	      // just passive discoverability for the tool-specific ones.
381	      const perTool = perToolPointers(skills, docs)
382	      let count = 0
383	      for (const t of tools) {
384	        const key = accessKey(conn.id, t.tool_name)
385	        // Already listed: an unbound upstream re-prepared by refresh().
386	        // Registering a duplicate name would throw.
387	        if (this.allowedToolKeys.has(key)) continue
388	        if (!isToolAllowed(acl.get(key), principals)) continue // hidden by ACL
389	        this.allowedToolKeys.add(key)
390	        this.registerTool(server, conn, t, perTool.get(t.tool_name) ?? [])
391	        count++
392	      }
393	      added.push({ slug: conn.slug, tools: count })
394	    }
395	    return { added, recovered }
396	  }

400	  /**
401	   * Precompute the upstream's first-result playbook hint at registration
402	   * (init and refresh both land here). No-op once the session has
403	   * delivered it — refresh() must not re-arm a received hint.
404	   */
405	  private armFirstResultHint(
406	    upstreamId: string,
407	    slug: string,
408	    skills: SkillForUpstreamRow[],
409	    docs: DocForUpstreamRow[]
410	  ): void {
411	    if (this.hintLedger.wasHinted(upstreamId)) return
412	    const hint = firstResultHint(slug, skills, docs)
413	    if (hint) this.firstResultHints.set(upstreamId, hint)
414	    else this.firstResultHints.delete(upstreamId)
415	  }
416	
417	  /**
418	   * Append the armed hint to a success surface as ONE extra first-party
419	   * text item, once per upstream per session. Runs AFTER the runner (so
420	   * after its sanitise pass) — the deliberate, bounded exception to
421	   * "success results are never augmented"; the append site is here, not
422	   * the runner, precisely so the ⟦ctxlayer⟧ marker survives without a
423	   * sanitiser carve-out. Hint bytes never enter respJson (usage stays
424	   * honest). Design: docs/plan/O-result-skill-hint.md.
425	   *
426	   * The hinted result also OMITS `structuredContent`: clients render the
427	   * structured value INSTEAD of the content array when both are present
428	   * (field-verified 2026-08-27 — the hint survived every server layer
429	   * including an SDK round-trip yet never reached the model on Driver/
430	   * Sentry, whose results carry structuredContent), which would make the
431	   * hint invisible on exactly the upstreams it was built for. The text
432	   * item carries the identical JSON, so the model loses nothing; only
433	   * this one result per upstream per session loses structured output.
434	   */
435	  private deliverFirstResultHint<
436	    T extends { content: Array<{ type: string; text?: string }>; structuredContent?: unknown }
437	  >(upstreamId: string, surface: T): T {
438	    const hint = this.firstResultHints.get(upstreamId)
439	    if (!hint) return surface
440	    this.hintLedger.markHinted(upstreamId)
441	    this.firstResultHints.delete(upstreamId)
442	    const { structuredContent: _omitted, ...rest } = surface
443	    return {
444	      ...rest,
445	      content: [...surface.content, { type: 'text', text: hint }]
446	    } as T
447	  }

449	  private resolveBearer(row: UpstreamServerRow, conn: UpstreamConnection): Promise<string | null> {
450	    return resolveUserUpstreamBearer(this.env, row, conn, this.userId)
451	  }

453	  /**
454	   * Resolve credentials, dial the upstream, and ensure its catalogue is
455	   * fresh. Returns null to skip the upstream (bad row, never-connected,
456	   * empty catalogue); throws propagate to the per-upstream catch in
457	   * `init` so one upstream's failure degrades only that upstream.
458	   *
459	   * `client: null` = list the tools without a client: the user HAS a
460	   * credential for this upstream but it yielded no bearer (flagged
461	   * reauth-required, or its refresh failed transiently just now). Skipping
462	   * it, as this used to, made the tools silently disappear. A user who
463	   * never connected the upstream still gets nothing listed — those tools
464	   * were never theirs to call.
465	   */
466	  private async prepareUpstream(
467	    row: UpstreamServerRow,
468	    cached: UpstreamToolRow[]
469	  ): Promise<{
470	    conn: UpstreamConnection
471	    row: UpstreamServerRow
472	    client: UpstreamClient | null
473	    tools: UpstreamToolRow[]
474	  } | null> {
475	    const conn = safeConnection(row)
476	    if (!conn) return null
477	    const bearer = await this.resolveBearer(row, conn)
478	    if (conn.authStrategy !== 'none' && bearer === null) {
479	      if (!isUserScoped(conn) || cached.length === 0) return null
480	      const cred = await getUserCredentialStatus(this.env, this.userId, conn.id)
481	      return cred.present ? { conn, row, client: null, tools: cached } : null
482	    }
483	
484	    const client = this.makeClient(conn, bearer)
485	    const tools = await this.ensureCatalogue(conn, client, cached)
486	    if (tools.length === 0) {
487	      // Empty even after refresh — log and skip; user sees built-ins only.
488	      console.warn(`upstream ${conn.slug} returned no tools after refresh`)
489	      await client.close()
490	      return null
491	    }
492	    return { conn, row, client, tools }
493	  }
494	
495	  /**
496	   * The client to call through, binding or REbinding it when needed:
497	   *   - no client yet (a listed-but-unbound upstream) → try to bind now, so a
498	   *     credential the user just re-authorized works on the very next call;
499	   *   - the stored credential changed since this client was bound (`cred`
500	   *     is the handler's per-call status read) → rebind onto the new token.
501	   * `cred` is null for shared/none strategies: nothing per-user to go stale.
502	   * A failed rebind falls back to the existing client rather than failing a
503	   * call that might still succeed. Concurrent calls share one in-flight bind.
504	   */
505	  private async ensureBound(
506	    conn: UpstreamConnection,
507	    cred: CredentialStatus | null
508	  ): Promise<UpstreamClient | null> {
509	    const current = this.clients.get(conn.id)
510	    if (current && (cred === null || cred.updatedAt === this.boundStamp.get(conn.id))) {
511	      return current
512	    }
513	    let inflight = this.binding.get(conn.id)
514	    if (!inflight) {
515	      inflight = this.bind(conn).finally(() => this.binding.delete(conn.id))
516	      this.binding.set(conn.id, inflight)
517	    }
518	    return (await inflight) ?? current ?? null
519	  }
520	
521	  private async bind(conn: UpstreamConnection): Promise<UpstreamClient | null> {
522	    const row = this.rows.get(conn.id)
523	    if (!row) return null
524	    try {
525	      const bearer = await this.resolveBearer(row, conn)
526	      if (conn.authStrategy !== 'none' && bearer === null) return null
527	      // Stamp AFTER resolving: the resolve itself may refresh + save.
528	      const stamp = isUserScoped(conn)
529	        ? (await getUserCredentialStatus(this.env, this.userId, conn.id)).updatedAt
530	        : null
531	      const client = this.makeClient(conn, bearer)
532	      // A superseded client is dropped, not closed: another in-flight call
533	      // may still be on it, and clients connect lazily / hold no socket
534	      // (same no-teardown stance as the class doc).
535	      this.clients.set(conn.id, client)
536	      this.boundStamp.set(conn.id, stamp)
537	      this.unbound.delete(conn.id)
538	      return client
539	    } catch (err) {
540	      console.error(`[upstream-proxy] ${conn.slug}: bind failed: ${errMessage(err)}`)
541	      return null
542	    }
543	  }

545	  private async ensureCatalogue(
546	    conn: UpstreamConnection,
547	    client: UpstreamClient,
548	    cached: UpstreamToolRow[]
549	  ): Promise<UpstreamToolRow[]> {
550	    // Staleness is derived from the prefetched rows (cached_at rides on
551	    // every row), so the fresh path costs no extra round trip.
552	    const cachedAt = cached.length === 0 ? null : Math.max(...cached.map((t) => t.cached_at))
553	    const stale = cachedAt === null || Date.now() / 1000 - cachedAt > CATALOGUE_TTL_SECONDS
554	    if (!stale) return cached
555	    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
556	    const outOfBudget = new Promise<'timeout'>((resolve) => {
557	      timer = setTimeout(() => resolve('timeout'), this.catalogueBudgetMs)
558	    })
559	    const outcome = await Promise.race([this.refreshCatalogue(conn, client), outOfBudget])
560	    clearTimeout(timer)
561	    if (outcome === 'timeout') {
562	      console.warn(
563	        `[catalogue] ${conn.slug}: tools/list still running after ${this.catalogueBudgetMs}ms — ` +
564	          'serving the cached catalogue; the refresh continues in the background'
565	      )
566	    }
567	    // Whatever the refresh did (or has not done yet), serve the cache —
568	    // stale beats nothing, and beats a reset session.
569	    return listCachedTools(this.env, conn.id)
570	  }
571	
572	  /** Fetch and store a fresh catalogue. Never throws: failures are logged. */
573	  private async refreshCatalogue(conn: UpstreamConnection, client: UpstreamClient): Promise<'done'> {
574	    try {
575	      // Reuse the persistent client this registry already opened — avoids
576	      // a second handshake just to fetch the catalogue.
577	      const tools = await client.listTools()
578	      const res = await replaceCachedTools(this.env, conn.id, tools)
579	      if (res.rejectedShrink) {
580	        console.warn(
581	          `[catalogue] ${conn.slug}: refresh returned ${res.rejectedShrink.incoming} tools vs ` +
582	            `${res.rejectedShrink.prior} cached — suspect shrink rejected, serving prior catalogue`
583	        )
584	      }
585	    } catch (err) {
586	      const msg = errMessage(err)
587	      console.error(`[catalogue] ${conn.slug}: tools/list failed: ${msg}`)
588	    }
589	    return 'done'
590	  }
591	
592	  private registerTool(
593	    server: McpServer,
594	    conn: UpstreamConnection,
595	    row: UpstreamToolRow,
596	    pointers: string[] = []
597	  ): void {
598	    const mangled = mangleToolName(conn.slug, row.tool_name)
599	    // Upstream-supplied descriptions are untrusted model input. Strip
600	    // control characters (which can hide injected instructions or
601	    // disrupt agent rendering) before forwarding. We deliberately do
602	    // NOT try to detect prompt-injection content — that's the model's
603	    // job; ours is to keep the wire bytes well-formed.
604	    let description = truncateDescription(
605	      sanitizeUntrustedText(`[${conn.displayName}] ${row.description ?? ''}`)
606	    )
607	    // Append org-curated per-tool attachment pointers. These are
608	    // first-party (slug strings we control), not upstream input, so they
609	    // need no sanitisation. Truncate the base description first to
610	    // reserve room — the pointer is the binding guidance and must
611	    // survive the 1024-char cap even when the upstream blurb is long.
612	    if (pointers.length > 0) {
613	      // Descriptive disclosure, NOT an imperative: name the org playbooks that
614	      // exist for this tool and leave the choice to the agent. The old
615	      // "consult X before using this tool" framing was a command smuggled
616	      // through the data plane — well-behaved agents (correctly) treat tool
617	      // metadata as untrusted and resist it, so it was both brittle and
618	      // eroding of the very boundary that protects callers from a malicious
619	      // upstream's descriptions. The structured home for these is
620	      // `describe_upstream` (per-tool `attached_skills`/`attached_docs`); this
621	      // line is just passive discoverability on the one field every client
622	      // renders. Wrapped in the ⟦ctxlayer⟧ provenance marker (first-party,
623	      // unforgeable — the upstream description above it is defanged).
624	      const suffix = `\n\n${firstParty(`Related org playbooks (optional context): ${pointers.join(', ')}.`)}`
625	      description = truncateDescription(description, 1024 - suffix.length) + suffix
626	    }
627	    let inputSchemaJson: unknown = {}
628	    try {
629	      inputSchemaJson = JSON.parse(row.input_schema)
630	    } catch {
631	      // Bad cache row; treat as no schema. Tool still callable.
632	    }
633	    const converted = jsonSchemaToZod(inputSchemaJson)
634	    const inputSchema = converted.shape ?? converted.zod
635	    // Close over the real upstream tool name from the cache row. The
636	    // mangled name we expose to the agent can drop the redundant
637	    // `${slug}-` prefix (see `mangleToolName`), so `unmangleToolName`
638	    // would no longer round-trip — we rely on `row.tool_name` here
639	    // instead. Sanity-check the mangled name shape only.
640	    const upstreamToolName = row.tool_name
641	    const handler = async (args: unknown, extra?: ProxyToolExtra) => {
642	      if (!unmangleToolName(mangled)) return errText(`bad tool name: ${mangled}`)
643	      // Defense-in-depth: only ACL-allowed tools are ever registered, so
644	      // this can't fire on the normal path. It backstops a future
645	      // refactor that registers more broadly. Generic code to the agent;
646	      // the real reason is logged server-side per the no-leak rule.
647	      if (!this.allowedToolKeys.has(accessKey(conn.id, upstreamToolName))) {
648	        console.warn(`[tool-acl] blocked ${conn.slug}.${upstreamToolName} for user ${this.userId}`)
649	        return errText('access_denied: tool restricted')
650	      }
651	      const t0 = Date.now()
652	      const reqJson = safeJson(args)
653	      let status: 'ok' | 'error' | 'timeout' = 'ok'
654	      let truncated = false
655	      let respJson = ''
656	      // Set only on failures — a coarse class + the raw detail (scrubbed
657	      // for storage in the `finally`). Drives the usage error table.
658	      let errorCode: string | undefined
659	      let errorDetail: string | undefined
660	      try {
661	        // A6: user-scoped creds are baked into the client at bind time — one
662	        // point-read per call so a mid-session disconnect / reauth flag
663	        // blocks now, not when the session dies. Also gates async SUBMITs
664	        // (below). Inside the try so the block is RECORDED: these calls used
665	        // to return before any usage row was staged, which kept the people
666	        // who most needed to re-authorize out of the Errors table.
667	        const fresh = await checkCredentialFreshness(this.env, this.userId, conn)
668	        if (fresh.error) {
669	          console.warn(
670	            `[cred-freshness] blocked ${conn.slug}.${upstreamToolName} for user ${this.userId}`
671	          )
672	          status = 'error'
673	          errorCode = 'credential_revoked'
674	          errorDetail = fresh.error
675	          return errText(fresh.error)
676	        }
677	        // Async-eligible tools (per `authConfig.asyncTools`) can run far
678	        // longer than an interactive client's request timeout — Claude
679	        // Desktop hard-caps at ~180s and does not reset on progress, so no
680	        // server-side keepalive helps. Run them out-of-band: enqueue a job,
681	        // return a token immediately, and let the ctxlayer-jobs consumer run
682	        // the full call (poll_task fetches the result). A retried identical
683	        // call returns the cached result. See docs/plan/I-upstream-resilience §I9.
684	        if (isAsyncTool(conn, upstreamToolName)) {
685	          try {
686	            const sub = await submitAsyncJob(
687	              this.env,
688	              {
689	                userId: this.userId,
690	                sessionId: this.sessionId,
691	                origin: await this.usageOrigin?.()
692	              },
693	              conn,
694	              upstreamToolName,
695	              args
696	            )
697	            respJson = sub.respJson
698	            // The ack is the first thing the agent reads for this
699	            // upstream — the poll_task replay stays byte-stable.
700	            return this.deliverFirstResultHint(conn.id, sub.surface)
701	          } catch (err) {
702	            // A failed submit (D1 insert, queue send) reaches the agent as a
703	            // thrown error — record it as one, not as a zero-byte 'ok'.
704	            status = 'error'
705	            errorDetail = errMessage(err)
706	            errorCode = classifyUpstreamError('error', errorDetail)
707	            throw err
708	          }
709	        }
710	        const client = await this.ensureBound(conn, fresh.status)
711	        if (!client) {
712	          // Credential on file and not flagged, yet no bearer came out of it:
713	          // its refresh failed for a (so far) transient reason. Say so — a
714	          // bare "not connected" reads as "reconnect the connector".
715	          const msg =
716	            `upstream_unavailable: could not establish your ${conn.slug} connection — ` +
717	            `refreshing its token failed just now, which is usually temporary. Nothing was ` +
718	            `sent to ${conn.slug}. Retry in a minute; if it keeps failing, the user should ` +
719	            `re-authorize it at ${spaUrl(this.env, UPSTREAMS_PAGE)}.`
720	          status = 'error'
721	          errorCode = 'upstream_auth'
722	          errorDetail = msg
723	          return errText(msg)
724	        }
725	        const outcome = await runUpstreamCall({
726	          slug: conn.slug,
727	          toolName: upstreamToolName,
728	          upstreamUrl: conn.url,
729	          maxResponseBytes: conn.authConfig.maxResponseBytes,
730	          run: () => callWithHeartbeat(extra, () => client.callTool(upstreamToolName, args))
731	        })
732	        respJson = outcome.respJson
733	        status = outcome.status
734	        truncated = outcome.truncated
735	        errorCode = outcome.errorCode
736	        errorDetail = outcome.errorDetail
737	        // First SUCCESSFUL result only: errors carry nudges/scrubbing and
738	        // "read the playbook" attached to a failure reads as blame; a
739	        // truncated result already carries the truncation notice (one
740	        // first-party segment per result). Neither consumes the hint.
741	        if (outcome.status === 'ok' && !outcome.truncated) {
742	          return this.deliverFirstResultHint(conn.id, outcome.surface)
743	        }
744	        return outcome.surface
745	      } finally {
746	        await this.stageUsage({
747	          userId: this.userId,
748	          sessionId: this.sessionId,
749	          upstreamId: conn.id,
750	          tool: mangled,
751	          reqJson,
752	          respJson,
753	          latencyMs: Date.now() - t0,
754	          status,
755	          truncated,
756	          errorCode,
757	          errorMessage: errorDetail != null ? scrubErrorForStorage(errorDetail) : undefined
758	        })
759	      }
760	    }
761	    // The SDK's `registerTool` overload requires a Zod schema at the
762	    // type level but happily accepts our derived shape at runtime.
763	    // Single cast on the call keeps the handler closed-over types
764	    // intact (alternative: cast the inputSchema to `never`, which
765	    // collapses the callback signature to `() => ...`).
766	    ;(
767	      server.registerTool as unknown as (
768	        name: string,
769	        cfg: { title: string; description: string; inputSchema: unknown },
770	        cb: (args: unknown, extra: ProxyToolExtra) => unknown
771	      ) => unknown
772	    )(
773	      mangled,
774	      // title = mangled so the human-facing label matches the
775	      // agent-callable name (and surfaces the upstream slug). Falls
776	      // out of the same `<slug>__<tool>` rule the admin upstreams
777	      // page's "Agent-visible name" column uses, after the redundant-
778	      // prefix collapse (`notion__search`, not `notion__notion-search`).
779	      { title: mangled, description, inputSchema },
780	      handler
781	    )
782	  }
783	}
784	
785	function safeConnection(row: UpstreamServerRow): UpstreamConnection | null {
786	  try {
787	    return toUpstreamConnection(row)
788	  } catch {
789	    return null
790	  }
791	}

/**
 * Once-per-session state for the first-result playbook hint
 * (docs/plan/O-result-skill-hint.md). McpSessionDO HIBERNATES between
 * requests, so in-memory registry state dies on every wake — field-caught
 * 2026-08-27: the hint fired on consecutive calls because each wake
 * re-ran init() and re-armed it. "Already hinted" therefore lives in the
 * session DO's own SQLite, the same home as the usage outbox. The
 * in-memory variant backs unit tests and the storage-less default.
 */

export interface HintLedger {
  wasHinted(upstreamId: string): boolean
  markHinted(upstreamId: string): void
}

export function inMemoryHintLedger(): HintLedger {
  const hinted = new Set<string>()
  return {
    wasHinted: (id) => hinted.has(id),
    markHinted: (id) => void hinted.add(id)
  }
}

/** Durable ledger in the session DO's SQLite — survives hibernation. */
export function sqliteHintLedger(sql: SqlStorage): HintLedger {
  sql.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hinted_upstreams (upstream_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY)`)
  return {
    wasHinted: (id) =>
      sql.exec(`SELECT 1 FROM hinted_upstreams WHERE upstream_id = ?`, id).toArray().length > 0,
    markHinted: (id) =>
      void sql.exec(`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO hinted_upstreams (upstream_id) VALUES (?)`, id)
  }
}

/**
 * The per-call gate. `error` is first-party guidance (no upstream input),
 * safe to surface. The recovery is a BROWSER step only the user can take, so
 * the text names the page and says to simply retry afterwards — the proxy
 * rebinds the upstream on the next call once a fresh credential is on file
 * (see `UpstreamProxyRegistry.ensureBound`); no reload_upstreams, and no
 * reconnect of the MCP connector, is needed.
 */
export async function checkCredentialFreshness(
  env: Env,
  userId: string,
  conn: FreshnessConn
): Promise<CredentialFreshness> {
  if (conn.authStrategy !== 'user_bearer' && conn.authStrategy !== 'user_oauth') {
    return { error: null, status: null }
  }
  const status = await getUserCredentialStatus(env, userId, conn.id)
  if (status.present && !status.needsReauth) return { error: null, status }
  const reason = status.present
    ? 'requires re-authorization (its authorization expired or was revoked, and could not be refreshed)'
    : 'has been disconnected'
  const upstreamsUrl = spaUrl(env, UPSTREAMS_PAGE)
  return {
    error:
      `credential_revoked: your ${conn.slug} connection ${reason}. ` +
      `Nothing was sent to ${conn.slug}. The user must re-authorize it at ${upstreamsUrl} — ` +
      `then just retry this call. Reconnecting this MCP connector does not fix it.`,
    status
  }
}

    it builds only what the request addresses and resolves the account,
    catalogue and credentials fresh each time.

  lane. Anything agent-facing must behave the same on both — built-in tools
  are lane-neutral definitions in `mcp/builtins/`, prompts/resources are
  written once against `mcp/surface.ts`, and proxied-tool presentation is in
  `mcp/proxied-tool.ts`. A new upstream-proxy behaviour has to be added to
  BOTH orchestrations (`mcp/proxy-registry.ts` and
  `mcp/stateless/upstream-tools.ts`). Usage events record the lane, so the
  admin Usage + Errors pages can compare them."""
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF

feat(mcp): stateless lane for protocol 2026-07-28, beside the session lane

/mcp is now one endpoint served by two coexisting lanes, routed per
request by protocol era (the MCP SDK's isLegacyRequest):

- session lane: 2025-era clients (initialize, Mcp-Session-Id), served
  unchanged by McpSessionDO on MCP SDK v1.
- stateless lane: protocol revision 2026-07-28, a fresh MCP SDK v2
  server per request (agents createMcpHandler, legacy: 'reject'). No
  Durable Object, no session. It registers only what the request
  addresses and resolves account status, catalogue and credentials
  fresh each time. Kill switch: MCP_STATELESS_LANE=off.

Both lanes are permanent; 2025-era clients are never routed to the
stateless lane.

Shared between the lanes, so the agent-facing surface cannot drift:
- mcp/builtins/: lane-neutral built-in tool definitions with a thin
  adapter per SDK and one usage recorder.
- mcp/surface.ts: prompt/resource registration written once (skills,
  docs, /draft-skill).
- mcp/proxied-tool.ts, mcp/catalogue-cache.ts: proxied tool
  presentation and catalogue freshness, extracted from the registry.

Stateless specifics: usage is sent straight to the queue; the
first-result playbook hint is once per (user, client, upstream) with a
12 h re-arm (migration 0042, nightly prune); reload_upstreams reports
current state, since nothing is cached to reload.

Lane monitoring: usage events record lane, protocol revision and
client name (migration 0041). Admin Usage gains a Protocol lanes
panel; Admin Errors gains a lane column and filter.

Deps: @modelcontextprotocol/server and client 2.4.0, zod ^4.2.

Tests: built-ins and the stateless lane are driven end to end through
real MCP SDK clients against D1 (the first suites to exercise /mcp
itself).

EOF

content.text:
Committed on `main` as `1d8e98f`; not pushed, not deployed.

I made it one commit rather than three: the phases overlap in the same files (`session-do.ts`, the usage pipeline, the registry), so splitting them cleanly wasn't possible without partial staging. The message describes the three parts separately. `.claude/settings.json` and `.entire/` are left out, as before.

The next step is the canary, in this order:

1. Apply migrations `0041` and `0042` on the dev tenant.
2. Release the dev tenant.
3. Connect your own Claude Desktop to it and check the Protocol lanes panel shows your calls under the stateless lane.

The ops template needs no change for this: the stateless lane is on by default, and `MCP_STATELESS_LANE` only has to be added there if you want the kill switch available per tenant.
